interval_rule: For each existing nominal leg direction a, preserve that direction and constrain hip=a-atan2(L*sin(k),U+L*cos(k)) and knee k to the existing joint bounds. Positive link lengths and 0<=k<=pi/2 make the hip offset monotone for either link-length ordering. Intersect the four resulting floor-relative torso-height intervals, using the measured body orientation and compiled anchors. Sixty-four bisection iterations retain the feasible endpoint when the hip bound restricts knee flexion; this is numerical geometry, not a behavioral tolerance.
height_rule: If the intersection is nonempty and the measured height is not below it, request min(measured height,common upper bound). Otherwise retain measured height and explicitly mark lowering unavailable. Never request a rise or claim an infeasible interval is supported.
phase_rule: Use the SAME post-gate phases used to generate the original command. Phases strictly after the existing 72-step swing end receive the stance-height request. Swing and swing-end recontact-hold phases retain the actual floor-relative measured height. This does not skip a contact gate, reset clocks, select a different first leg, cache contact, or change timeouts.
reference_rule: Keep the V34 floor context and source/session continuity, existing swing composition, joint projections, first neutral reference, reference slew, feedback gains and motor limits. Per-limb reference height and scheduled phase are retained. Nominal support residual remains relative to the ACTUAL measured torso pose, not a claim that the requested body height has been achieved.
infeasibility_rule: An empty joint-compatible height intersection or a measured height below the intersection prevents the lowering correction but retains the bounded V34-style floor targets and residuals. Nonfinite or non-downward geometry, nominal directions outside hip bounds, invalid links, or knee limits outside the declared monotone domain fail closed before issuing motion.
physical_limit: Kinematic reference proposal, not contact-force control, guaranteed body lowering, native load support, stability, successful walking or an alternative-trajectory prediction. Brief loss of support, body-height tracking and landing tracking require a fresh bounded physical attempt.
